ECG signals are preprocessed using a 0.5-50 Hz bandpass filter and power line interference is removed with a 50/60 Hz adaptive notch filter. R-peaks are detected using the Pan-Tompkins algorithm with adaptive thresholding. Ectopic beats and artifacts are identified and corrected using the method of non-linear predictive interpolation. Normal-to-normal (NN) intervals are calculated from the corrected R-peak series. Time-domain HRV measures including SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50, and triangular index are extracted from the NN intervals. Frequency-domain analysis is performed using Lomb-Scargle periodogram to avoid resampling, with power calculated in VLF (0.003-0.04 Hz), LF (0.04-0.15 Hz), and HF (0.15-0.4 Hz) bands. Non-linear features including sample entropy, approximate entropy, Poincaré plot metrics (SD1, SD2), and detrended fluctuation analysis scaling exponents are computed. Results are normalized to subject baseline and visualized with time plots and heat maps.

Feature selection is performed using recursive feature elimination with cross-validation. Selected features are standardized using z-score normalization and fed into an ensemble of classifiers (SVM, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting) for arrhythmia classification.

Multiple leads are analyzed independently and results are combined using rule-based logic for spatial information integration. A clinical risk score is calculated based on the morphological deviations from reference templates.

Continuous ECG signals are acquired and initially filtered with a 0.5-40 Hz bandpass filter. Power line interference is removed using a notch filter centered at 50/60 Hz. An adaptive baseline removal algorithm corrects for baseline drift. The signal is segmented into 30-second non-overlapping windows. For each window, QRS complexes are detected using the Hamilton-Tompkins algorithm. Signal quality is assessed using metrics such as kurtosis, baseline deviation, and signal-to-noise ratio. Windows with low quality are marked for more intensive processing. Subsampling is applied to high-quality segments, reducing the sampling rate from 250 Hz to 50 Hz. A beat template is created by aligning and averaging selected normal beats. For each new beat, a similarity score to the template is calculated. Beats with low similarity undergo full feature extraction, while similar beats use lightweight processing. Heart rate is continuously calculated using a 10-second moving window with 50% overlap. Significant changes in heart rate or beat morphology trigger alerts via the monitoring system.
